newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IMF says positive on Hong Kong's economic outlook.
newsitem.headline: IMF says positive on Hong Kong's economic outlook.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said uncertainties over Hong Kong's transition in 1997 were reduced significantly in the past year and it has found widely held confidence over the territory's prospects.

"Current macroeconomic conditions provide a conducive environment for a smooth political transition," an IMF mission said in a statement provided by the Hong Kong government on Wednesday following an annual consultation in the territory.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight next June 30 after a century and a half as a British territory.
The IMF said Hong Kong's real gross domestic product (GDP) was seen at 4.5 to 4.75 percent in 1996. A recovery was underway and should support growth of five to 5.25 percent in 1997, it said.
In line with this forecast, inflation in 1997 was likely to rise to a moderate seven percent, the IMF said.
But it cautioned that the pace of recovery could be affected by increases in U.S. interest rates or if economic activity in China decelerates.
The IMF mission also said the linked exchange rate system had played a critical role in promoting economic stability and engendering confidence over the years of the transition.
Hong Kong has pegged its dollar to the U.S. dollar at the HK$7.80 level since 1983.

"Hong Kong's medium-term prospects appear highly favourable given its proven track record of macroeconomics management, flexible markets, and its advantages of location which allow it to benefit from the huge growth potential of China," the IMF statement said.
